A.explanation: At $60 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, $F = P/v = 300000/60 = 5000 \text{ N} = 5 \text{ kN}$, which balances the resistive force at constant speed.

B.explanation: Gives twice the correct force, possibly from an error dividing $300 \text{ kW}$ by $30$ instead of $60 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: Much too large, possibly from multiplying $300 \text{ kW}$ and $60 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ incorrectly instead of using $F = P/v$.

D.explanation: Much too large, from confusing power and force and mishandling the $300 \text{ kW}$ and $60 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ values.

hints: Notice the car moves at a constant speed of $60 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so the forward driving force must exactly balance the total resistive force.
Recall the power relation for motion against a force at speed $v$: $P = Fv$, where $P$ must be in watts and $F$ in newtons.
Convert $300 \text{ kW}$ to $300000 \text{ W}$ and divide by $60 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find $F$ in newtons, then convert to $\text{kN}$.
walkthrough: At constant speed the acceleration is zero, so resultant force is zero and the engine driving force $F$ equals the total resistive force.
Useful power is given by $P = Fv$ for a force $F$ moving at steady speed $v$.
Substitute $P = 300 \text{ kW} = 300000 \text{ W}$ and $v = 60 \text{ m s}^{-1}$: $F = 300000/60 = 5000 \text{ N}$.
Convert to kilonewtons: $5000 \text{ N} = 5 \text{ kN}$, so the resistive force is $5 \text{ kN}$. This is option A.
